module_title: Major Fairs of UP - Foundational Matrix (Kumbh, Nauchandi & Bateshwar)
introduction: Uttar Pradesh hosts approximately 2,250 fairs annually (the highest number being in Mathura). At this foundational level, we will focus on the top 5 historic and culturally massive fairs that are the absolute baseline for any UP state exam.

core_concepts.title: Kumbh Mela - Prayagraj
core_concepts.description:
- **Location:** Prayagraj (At the confluence/Sangam of the Ganga, Yamuna, and the mythical Saraswati).
- **Frequency:** Maha Kumbh occurs every 12 years, and Ardh Kumbh every 6 years (Next Maha Kumbh is scheduled for 2025).
- **Significance:** The world's largest peaceful religious gathering. It is officially recognized in UNESCO's list of 'Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity'.

core_concepts.title: Nauchandi Mela - Meerut
core_concepts.description:
- **Location:** Meerut.
- **Significance:** A magnificent symbol of Hindu-Muslim communal harmony. The fair is uniquely held at a site where the Nauchandi Devi Temple and the Dargah of Bala Mian are situated directly opposite each other.

core_concepts.title: Bateshwar Mela - Agra
core_concepts.description:
- **Location:** Agra (on the banks of the Yamuna River at Bateshwar).
- **Significance:** It is one of the most famous **Animal Fairs (Pashu Mela)** in Uttar Pradesh, particularly renowned for the trading of camels and horses.

core_concepts.title: Syed Salar Mela - Bahraich
core_concepts.description:
- **Location:** Bahraich.
- **Significance:** Held at the revered dargah (tomb) of the warrior-saint Syed Salar Masud Ghazi (often referred to locally as Ghazi Mian).

core_concepts.title: Deva Sharif Mela - Barabanki
core_concepts.description:
- **Location:** Barabanki.
- **Significance:** An annual Urs (commemoration) held at the shrine of the renowned Sufi saint **Haji Waris Ali Shah**. It attracts devotees from across the subcontinent.

important_entities.name: Mathura
important_entities.significance: If an exam asks which district hosts the maximum number of fairs in UP, the answer is Mathura (around 86 fairs annually), followed by Kanpur and Hamirpur. Pilibhit hosts the fewest.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
Students frequently confuse the locations of the two major Sufi shrines. Memorize this exact mapping to avoid negative marking: 
1. **Syed Salar Masud Ghazi** = Bahraich
2. **Haji Waris Ali Shah (Deva Sharif)** = Barabanki

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Since Agra borders Rajasthan (which has a desert climate), it logically hosts UP's biggest camel and livestock trading event—the Bateshwar Animal Fair.

exam_strategy_tips: In UP Police Constable and UPSSSC PET exams, 'Nauchandi Mela' (Meerut) and 'Deva Sharif' (Barabanki) are the most recycled one-liner questions. Lock these in your memory as absolute facts.
